newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index boosted by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index boosted by blue chips.

text.p: Slovakia's official SAX index firmed 2.31 points to 169.55 in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, boosted by gains to several blue chips.
Overall, both volume and turnover rose sharply after a dull week, driven by a direct deal in Benzinol, the country's major petrol fuels distributor.
The issue traded 764,139 shares at 505 crowns, representing some 29.9 percent of the company's basic capital. Traders said they were uncertain on the deal's background.
"We should know more about this in a short time," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
Some brokers said the move might have been still only a transfer between the accounts of some of Benzinol's major owners, without changing the company's ownership structure.

Benzinol is controlled by oil refinery Slovnaft which owns 51 percent. The second major owner is the country's largest savings bank, Slovenska Sporitelna, with some 34 percent. Other shareholders own less than 29.9 percent in the company.
"If it was a normal deal, one of these two biggest owners would dramatically cut its stake," Sykora added.
Trading on the bourse's floor was dominated by steel maker VSZ, which traded 3,447 shares and rose 10 crowns to 650.
The heaviest gains were recorded at drug maker Slovakofarma, which added 380 crowns to 4,180, on 500 traded shares.
Overall, volume climbed to 960,810 shares, from 49,611 shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover increased to 448.46 million crowns from 43.1 million.
